What's So Bad about the Galactic Empire? | FEE

Liberal claptrap. And the author obviously doesn't know shit about Star Wars.

The Expanded Universe goes into GREAT detail on the differences between the Old Republic, The Galactic Empire, and the New Republic.

Now, the first thing to know is that the Galaxy in Star Wars is not a monolithic political body. There are vast territories that are NOT part of The Republic or The Empire. These areas are often unexplored, and home to dangerous pirates, raiders, aliens, etc. While planets near the Core Systems (relatively near to the Capitol of The Republic/Empire located at Coruscant) were kept relatively safe from such dangers; planets near The Outer Rim were often attacked and raided.

The Old Republic and its bloated bureaucracy rarely lent military aid to protect these worlds (The Jedi were also rarely to be found when needed) leaving them open to attack. The Empire, in contrast, had a policy of keeping a military presence in ALL of its territories, including The Outer Rim.

Also, in The Old Republic, The Galactic Senate had very little say over the internal workings of member worlds. This led to widespread and common violations of Sentients' Rights. Slavery, in particular, was VERY common, often with the tacit support of The Senate, itself. Furthermore, despite being the most populous and common species in The Galaxy, humans were often the targets of discrimination, oppression, and slavery in worlds controlled by non-human aliens.

This is, again, in contrast to The Empire that had very pro-human policies, and even outlawed slavery (although certain aliens were still, secretly, used as slave labor by The Imperial Military. This was justified with the explanation that they had rebelled against the Empire and so had forfeited their rights.) Furthermore, The Moffs (Regional Governors) were under explicit orders from The Emperor to standardize law and order across The Empire, which was said to have improved the standard of living for a majority of its citizens.

As far as smuggling goes, the only things ever explicitly stated to be common smugglers' fare were illegal drugs (spice, death sticks, etc) or contraband weapons. That shipment of Jabba's that Han Solo dumped when he got boarded by Imperial Officers? Yeah, that was a large shipment of Spice. Han Solo was nothing more than a drug runner, before joining the Rebellion.

There's a LOT more that I could go into, but you get the just of it. By most measures, The Empire was FAAAR superior to The Old Republic at providing peace and prosperity to its citizens.

Thanks for your insight, it appears that the author is only weighing on on the movies rather than the expanded universe including books, etc. Just like with the Halo franchise, beneath the games is a tremendous amount of information and unexplored stories that the game player would never know until they read the books.
